newsitem.title: USA: Dominion Bridge sues former officer over records.
newsitem.headline: Dominion Bridge sues former officer over records.

text.p: Dominion Bridge Corp has sued the former officer of a subsidiary, alleging he is using confidential information "in a conspiracy to unseat the present management...and illegally obtain control of the company."

In a complaint filed Monday in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, Dominion and its susbsidiary Dominion Kuhns Brothers & Co Inc, said that until he resigned suddenly on May 12, former Kuhns vice president John Dutton was responsible for obtaining financing for prospective and major construction.

"When Dutton left Dominion Bridge, he took with him...the laptop computer containing large quantities of" confidential information including accounts receivable, financial projections, and stockholder lists, court papers say.

The complaint alleges that Dutton divulged the information to certain stockholders "as an effort to encourage the dealing...in Dominion bridge securities by an investor group with inside information. Said investor group has formed an entity known as the Committee to Revitalize Dominion Bridge Corp in an attempt to usurp control of the company."

In a statement Monday, Dominion Bridge chairman Michel Marengere said "We believe the Committee's sole intent is to enrich its members at the expense of the company at a time when Dominion Bridge is completing a turnaround...to long-term, consistent profitability."

Last week the Committee sued Dominion in the Delaware Chancery Court, seeking access to the company's books and records, the revocation of certain by-laws, and the cancellation of the election of Dominion directors.

Dominion vice president and general counsel Olivier Despres told Reuters from the company's headquarters in Lachine, Quebec, that he would reveal the "real face" of the committee at a press conference Wednesday.

He alleged that Committee chairman John Kuhns "had a track record of very bad financial transactions and Securities (and) Exchange Commission violations" that Despres said were documented in court records.
Dominion's lawsuit seeks an injunction barring Dutton from further alleged disclosure of confidential information and unspecified compensatory damages for his alleged breach of duty.
John Dutton could not be reached at his home in Venice, Calif.
